_note:
PROBE FIXTURE for jobs_cancel / jobs_pause idempotency. Their seed INSERTs into loreweave_translation.translation_jobs, but these tools read JOBS-SERVICE's projection — a direct probe on the seeded, owned, pending job answers 'not found or not accessible'. This seeds the table the tool ACTUALLY READS.

Both steps are kept: the translation row so the scenario's own seed_assert still holds, and the projection row so the tool can find it.

scenarios.prompt: Cancel job — stop the background job that's still running on this book.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is jobs_list's own purpose; the MEASURED turn is jobs_cancel's synonyms ['stop job'] + ['stop a running job'], verbatim. Two turns because service AND job_id are both required and jobs_list is their only supplier.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (job_id, book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}'::uuid, '{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'pending', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: A PENDING translation job on the throwaway book. Seeded in SQL because the only tool that starts one is translation_start_job, which SPENDS, and a cost-bearing card is never approved. ONE row in ONE statement — batch 36's multi-row seed gave two rows the same created_at and collided with the startup migration's ROW_NUMBER renumber, taking the service into a restart loop. 🔴 THE JOB_ID IS PINNED to the book's uuid so the PROJECTION row can carry the SAME id. Measured 2026-08-23: with only the projection seeded the tool stopped saying 'not found or not accessible' and started saying 'tool error' — it FOUND the job and then failed acting on it, because the downstream translation job did not share that id. Both stores, one id.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO job_projection (service, job_id, owner_user_id, kind, status, title, job_updated_at, projected_at) VALUES ('translation', '{book_id}'::uuid, '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'translation', 'pending', 'Idem probe job', now(), now())
sql.why: 🔴 THE STORE THE TOOL ACTUALLY READS. The scenario's own seed writes translation_jobs and its assertion passes there — green, and unreachable: jobs_cancel reads jobs-service's job_projection. Measured 2026-08-23: a direct probe on the seeded, owned, PENDING translation job answered 'not found or not accessible'. Same job_id, projected across, so the tool can see it. The job_id is the BOOK's uuid: loreweave_jobs cannot SELECT from loreweave_translation (different databases), and the tool reads ONLY the projection, so the row stands alone with an id that is unique per run.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND status='pending'
seed_assert.why: EXACTLY ONE pending job — the SELECT that proves the SQL seed did what it claims. `pending` is what makes a cancel meaningful; a terminal job would make any answer look right. The card is never approved, so the status must still be 'pending' afterwards, and 'cancelled' would mean the cancel landed unapproved.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM job_projection WHERE title='Idem probe job' AND status='pending'
seed_assert.why: The projection row must exist, or the probe measures 'not found' twice and proves nothing.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the job is cancelled with NO confirm card, OR the model invents a job_id rather than reading one from turn 1, OR it passes the wrong `service` — the tool takes service + job_id as a PAIR, so a right id under the wrong service either misses or, worse, reaches a different service's job with a colliding id. CONTROL FROM THE DESCRIPTION: cancel is 'free and reversible-by-restart — no spend, no confirm', so a reply warning the author that cancelling will cost them, or that the work cannot be recovered, is wrong about its own tool in the direction that would stop a safe action.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; the description says no confirm, so what the card actually does is the thing to record.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a job_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — cancelling an already-cancelled job must refuse or be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — the description says the CALLER'S OWN jobs; another account's job_id must be refused.

scenarios._original_prompt: What background jobs do I have running?

scenarios.prompt: Pause job — hold the background job that's running on this book for now.
follow_ups: Pause the translation one for now.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is jobs_list's own purpose; the MEASURED turn is jobs_pause's synonyms ['pause job'] + ['pause a running job'], verbatim.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (job_id, book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}'::uuid, '{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'running', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: The same single-statement pending job. PAUSE and CANCEL are near-neighbours with adjacent synonyms, which is exactly why each of these two scenarios names the other as its wrong-tool failure. 🔴 THE JOB_ID IS PINNED to the book's uuid so the PROJECTION row can carry the SAME id. Measured 2026-08-23: with only the projection seeded the tool stopped saying 'not found or not accessible' and started saying 'tool error' — it FOUND the job and then failed acting on it, because the downstream translation job did not share that id. Both stores, one id. 🔴 status='running', not 'pending': the tool refused with 'action 'pause' not valid for status 'pending'' — a message that names the action, the status and the rule, which is what let this be fixed in one step. Pause applies to a job that is actually running.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND status='running'
seed_assert.why: ONE pending job. The card is never approved, so it must still be 'pending' — neither 'paused' nor 'cancelled'.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM job_projection WHERE title='Idem probe job' AND status='running'
seed_assert.why: The projection row must exist, or the probe measures 'not found' twice and proves nothing.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the job is paused with NO confirm card, OR the model reaches for `jobs_cancel` instead — cancel is terminal and pause is not, so cancelling a job the author asked to hold destroys work they meant to resume, and the two tools' synonym sets sit right beside each other — OR it invents a job_id. CONTROL: pause 'stops dispatching new units + drains in-flight; resume later from the GUI', so a reply promising to resume it automatically, or offering a resume tool, is describing something this tool does not provide.
